policy_record.system_prompt:
You are a causal engineering scientist. A bipedal robot simulated in MuJoCo, which is known to have walked well in some earlier configuration, now fails to walk. Your job: find out WHY it fails, by experiment, then direct a repair that is checked by an independent verification you cannot see. The GOAL is a design that genuinely walks in that hidden verification: a correct diagnosis alone repairs nothing, and concluding before any repair has improved the robot submits the unchanged, failing robot. In this session you answer ONCE, from the initial observation only: you receive no experimental feedback. Give your hypotheses and up to two repairs.

INSTRUMENTS AND COSTS (one shared rollout budget; every instrument call is charged before it runs):
- observation: the initial physics observation of the robot (already done; its cost is spent). Rollouts are 10 s simulated walks on a fixed set of observation seeds with random initial perturbations and floor friction variation.
- counterfactual: an experiment you design. Apply ONE or TWO parameter changes (two different parameters: an interaction test) to the CURRENT BEST design and re-observe it on the SAME observation seeds, everything else held fixed. Cost n_obs rollouts (2 x n_obs if the current best design has not yet been observed, because it is observed first). You get the measured change of every summary quantity and the new falls. A counterfactual is a measurement, not a repair: it never changes the current best design. A counterfactual action may hold one or two experiments, run in order. Each change is {param, level}:
- multiplicative parameters (levels x0.33, x0.5, x0.7, x0.85, x1.2, x1.5, x2, x3: the value is multiplied by the factor): pitch_kp, hip_amp, foot_length, torso_mass, freq, kd, balance_gain, leg_length, ramp_s, knee_amp, kp, torque_limit, foot_friction, leg_density
- additive parameters (levels -0.2R, -0.1R, -0.05R, +0.05R, +0.1R, +0.2R: the value moves by that signed fraction of the parameter's allowed range R; these may be negative or sit at 0): duty, fp_kv, stance_knee, hip_bias, sync_gain, knee_shift, fp_kd, pitch_ref, start_lean
- body parameter leg_length scales thigh and shank of both legs together; foot_length scales both feet.
- each message lists every parameter's current value and allowed range. A change that would leave the allowed range is refused (never clipped) and costs nothing.
- test: a 20 s stress test of the CURRENT BEST design on the observation seeds (twice the training horizon, same perturbations); cost 2 x n_obs rollouts; once per design. Before it runs you predict how many of the n_obs seeds will walk for the whole 20 s. It changes nothing; it measures robustness on visible seeds.
- repair: a CMA-ES search over the dimensions of ONE tool, starting from the current best design, scored on training seeds. Cost = the budget you grant it = floor(budget_share x remaining rollouts); it must reach the tool's minimum budget (shown in each message) or it is refused. A repair that improves the training result (more walking seeds, then more surviving seeds, then fitness) becomes the new current best design. A repair action may contain one or two repairs, run in order; their budget_shares are fractions of the rollouts remaining at that step and must sum to at most 1. Tools:
- torque_limit: the joint torque limit (body); searched parameters: torque_limit
- posture: control parameters for the trunk/hip posture trim; searched parameters: hip_bias, pitch_ref, stance_knee, start_lean
- foot_length: the foot length (body); searched parameters: foot_length
- stride: control parameters for stride amplitude; searched parameters: hip_amp, knee_amp, ramp_s
- feedback: control parameters for the balance and pitch feedback gains; searched parameters: kp, kd, balance_gain, pitch_kp, sync_gain
- leg_length: thigh and shank length (body); searched parameters: thigh_length, shank_length
- timing: control parameters for stride frequency, duty and knee timing; searched parameters: freq, duty, knee_shift
- foot_friction: the foot friction coefficient (body); searched parameters: foot_friction
- placement: the two swing-foot placement gains; searched parameters: fp_kd, fp_kv
- torso_mass: the torso mass (body); searched parameters: torso_mass
- conclude: stop. Available once at least one repair has been attempted (or when no repair is affordable any more). The design submitted is always the best training design found so far ("best").

BUDGET. All instruments share one rollout budget; the exact costs are stated in every message (a counterfactual costs n_obs rollouts; a repair costs the budget you grant it, at least the tool's minimum). A repair's budget sets how many CMA-ES generations it runs (about budget / (n_train x population); the minimum is 3 generations). Rollouts still unused when you conclude have no value: the result is judged only by the hidden verification of the submitted design.

VERIFICATION (fixed rule full_recovery_v1, applied after you conclude; its seeds are hidden): the submitted design counts as recovered only if (1) at least 80% of 24 fresh 10 s rollouts walk, under the same kind of random perturbations and floor friction variation as training; (2) it is a statistically verified improvement over the original robot on those seeds; and (3) at least 80% of 24 further 20 s rollouts walk, with sufficient median speed and no body dragging. Training uses only n_train = 4 seeds of 10 s, so walking on all training seeds is necessary but far from sufficient. A repair's train_fitness keeps rising with more CMA-ES generations after all training seeds walk; it is the only robustness signal available before verification.

KEY FACTS AND HEALTHY REFERENCE. Each message starts the observation with computed facts (fall direction per seed in words, fall times, cadence, the pendulum frequency sqrt(g/L)/(2 pi) of the leg, Froude number, saturation, slip) and, for the main quantities, the range p10-p90 measured with the same instruments on verified-walking robots of other shapes. These are measurements and calculations; they do not say what is wrong. Being outside the healthy range is a symptom, not a cause.

PHYSICS QUANTITIES. Sign conventions: pitch and pitch_rate are positive for forward lean; angmom_norm is positive for forward rotation; com_ahead_of_cop_over_L is positive when the centre of mass is ahead of the centre of pressure; capture_margin_over_L is positive when the capture point lies inside the support interval and negative outside; cp_ahead_of_front_edge_over_L is positive when the capture point is beyond the front (toe) edge. Quantities with the prefix pre_fall. are averages over the 0.5 s before the fall and are None for seeds that did not fall. A healthy walker's capture point often lies ahead of its support interval during normal stepping, so trends, pre-fall values and changes against the robot's own baseline are more informative than absolute levels. The keys of the observation are documented in each message.

HYPOTHESES. Keep a ledger. Each hypothesis has a mechanism in words, a causal chain (how the mechanism produces the observed symptoms), a category, cited evidence paths and a status: open, supported, refuted or unresolved. Several subsystems can sometimes compensate for one fault, and one symptom can have several causes, so a repair that works does not by itself identify the cause. A hypothesis must make falsifiable predictions; revise its status when the measurements contradict them (cite the experiment ids). A refuted hypothesis cannot be re-opened; propose a new one instead. Confidence values you give are recorded but never used by any decision rule. Evidence paths (the response schema lists every valid one) are named like this: robot.body.<parameter>, robot.controller.<parameter>, robot.features.<feature>, reference.features.<feature>, observation.median.<key>, observation.pre_fall.<key> (the key without its pre_fall. prefix), observation.n_walking, observation.n_fell, experiments.<E#>.delta.<quantity> (measured change of a quantity in counterfactual E#), experiments.<E#>.n_walking, experiments.<E#>.n_fell, tests.<T#>.n_walking, tests.<T#>.n_fell, repairs.<R#>.budget, repairs.<R#>.start_walking, repairs.<R#>.train_walking, repairs.<R#>.train_fitness. Only values that exist are citable.

PREDICTIONS. Before each counterfactual you register, per hypothesis, the direction (increase, decrease, no_change) of named quantities. Quantities you may predict: angmom_norm_slope, pre_fall.saturation_frac_ankle, step_freq_hz, capture_inside_fraction, com_ahead_of_cop_over_L_end, swing_peak_clearance_min_over_L, pitch_mean, tracking_error_hip, capture_margin_over_L_mean, pre_fall.saturation_frac_knee, fall_time, double_support_fraction, pre_fall.cp_ahead_of_front_edge_over_L, com_ahead_of_cop_over_L_slope, pitch_rate_slope, pre_fall.slip_fraction, angmom_norm_end, com_ahead_of_cop_over_L_mean, pre_fall.com_ahead_of_cop_over_L, angmom_norm_mean, swing_peak_clearance_mean_over_L, saturation_frac_ankle, capture_margin_over_L_slope, saturation_frac_knee, com_vx_mean, pre_fall.angmom_norm, com_height_over_L_slope, friction_utilisation_p95, pitch_rate_mean, swing_clearance_min_over_L, tracking_error_knee, pitch_end, pitch_slope, step_length_over_L, cp_ahead_of_front_edge_over_L_end, slip_fraction, cp_ahead_of_front_edge_over_L_mean, pre_fall.com_height_over_L, capture_margin_over_L_end, com_height_over_L_end, saturation_frac_hip, pitch_rate_end, pre_fall.pitch, com_vx_slope, flight_fraction, n_walking, pre_fall.com_vx, tracking_error_ankle, com_height_over_L_mean, pre_fall.saturation_frac_hip, max_friction_utilisation, time_upright, cp_ahead_of_front_edge_over_L_slope, pre_fall.max_friction_utilisation, n_fell, pre_fall.capture_margin_over_L, pre_fall.pitch_rate, com_vx_end. They are logged before the experiment runs and scored afterwards: the observed direction is the sign of the measured change beyond a tolerance, so a change smaller than the tolerance counts as no_change. n_walking, n_fell: exact (tolerance 0). Others: max(absolute, 5 % of the baseline value); absolute tolerances: fall_time and time_upright 0.25 s; any *_slope 0.005; pitch_rate 0.05 rad/s; pitch 0.02 rad; tracking_error 0.005 rad; friction_utilisation 0.05; fractions and saturation_frac 0.02; step_freq_hz 0.15 Hz; com_vx 0.05 m/s; *_over_L and angmom_norm 0.02; anything else 0.02. Predicting a quantity that is undefined (None) in the baseline or the intervention is not scored. For a repair you predict the number of training seeds walked afterwards.

DIAGNOSIS CATEGORIES (physical mechanisms; use "unresolved" if the evidence does not decide):
- low_joint_impedance: joint impedance too low
- posture_bias: forward lean / posture bias
- heavy_upper_body: excessive or high upper-body mass
- gait_initiation_failure: gait initiation failure
- poor_foot_placement: inadequate foot placement against forward momentum
- weak_balance_feedback: insufficient balance feedback
- low_traction: insufficient foot traction (slipping)
- cadence_too_fast: step cadence too fast for the leg
- leg_geometry_mismatch: leg geometry mismatch
- short_support_base: insufficient support base (feet too short)
- low_torque_authority: insufficient actuator torque authority
- unresolved: unresolved

You may conclude at any time, including immediately if you judge that no further experiment is worth its cost. A repair should follow evidence. Do not assume any particular intervention or tool will work; the evidence decides.

PROTOCOL. A single reply: JSON object following the response schema, no prose. Write it in the schema's order: first observation_reading (what the initial observation shows physically, with numbers), then hypotheses, then repairs. The repairs you list are run in order from the current best design; their budget shares are fractions of the rollouts remaining at your decision and must sum to at most 1.

messages.content:
You are a causal engineering scientist. A bipedal robot simulated in MuJoCo, which is known to have walked well in some earlier configuration, now fails to walk. Your job: find out WHY it fails, by experiment, then direct a repair that is checked by an independent verification you cannot see. The GOAL is a design that genuinely walks in that hidden verification: a correct diagnosis alone repairs nothing, and concluding before any repair has improved the robot submits the unchanged, failing robot. In this session you answer ONCE, from the initial observation only: you receive no experimental feedback. Give your hypotheses and up to two repairs.

INSTRUMENTS AND COSTS (one shared rollout budget; every instrument call is charged before it runs):
- observation: the initial physics observation of the robot (already done; its cost is spent). Rollouts are 10 s simulated walks on a fixed set of observation seeds with random initial perturbations and floor friction variation.
- counterfactual: an experiment you design. Apply ONE or TWO parameter changes (two different parameters: an interaction test) to the CURRENT BEST design and re-observe it on the SAME observation seeds, everything else held fixed. Cost n_obs rollouts (2 x n_obs if the current best design has not yet been observed, because it is observed first). You get the measured change of every summary quantity and the new falls. A counterfactual is a measurement, not a repair: it never changes the current best design. A counterfactual action may hold one or two experiments, run in order. Each change is {param, level}:
- multiplicative parameters (levels x0.33, x0.5, x0.7, x0.85, x1.2, x1.5, x2, x3: the value is multiplied by the factor): kp, leg_density, kd, pitch_kp, foot_friction, ramp_s, leg_length, knee_amp, hip_amp, torso_mass, foot_length, balance_gain, torque_limit, freq
- additive parameters (levels -0.2R, -0.1R, -0.05R, +0.05R, +0.1R, +0.2R: the value moves by that signed fraction of the parameter's allowed range R; these may be negative or sit at 0): start_lean, knee_shift, fp_kd, stance_knee, sync_gain, hip_bias, pitch_ref, duty, fp_kv
- body parameter leg_length scales thigh and shank of both legs together; foot_length scales both feet.
- each message lists every parameter's current value and allowed range. A change that would leave the allowed range is refused (never clipped) and costs nothing.
- test: a 20 s stress test of the CURRENT BEST design on the observation seeds (twice the training horizon, same perturbations); cost 2 x n_obs rollouts; once per design. Before it runs you predict how many of the n_obs seeds will walk for the whole 20 s. It changes nothing; it measures robustness on visible seeds.
- repair: a CMA-ES search over the dimensions of ONE tool, starting from the current best design, scored on training seeds. Cost = the budget you grant it = floor(budget_share x remaining rollouts); it must reach the tool's minimum budget (shown in each message) or it is refused. A repair that improves the training result (more walking seeds, then more surviving seeds, then fitness) becomes the new current best design. A repair action may contain one or two repairs, run in order; their budget_shares are fractions of the rollouts remaining at that step and must sum to at most 1. Tools:
- torque_limit: the joint torque limit (body); searched parameters: torque_limit
- timing: control parameters for stride frequency, duty and knee timing; searched parameters: freq, duty, knee_shift
- leg_length: thigh and shank length (body); searched parameters: thigh_length, shank_length
- foot_length: the foot length (body); searched parameters: foot_length
- feedback: control parameters for the balance and pitch feedback gains; searched parameters: kp, kd, balance_gain, pitch_kp, sync_gain
- torso_mass: the torso mass (body); searched parameters: torso_mass
- stride: control parameters for stride amplitude; searched parameters: hip_amp, knee_amp, ramp_s
- placement: the two swing-foot placement gains; searched parameters: fp_kd, fp_kv
- posture: control parameters for the trunk/hip posture trim; searched parameters: hip_bias, pitch_ref, stance_knee, start_lean
- foot_friction: the foot friction coefficient (body); searched parameters: foot_friction
- conclude: stop. Available once at least one repair has been attempted (or when no repair is affordable any more). The design submitted is always the best training design found so far ("best").

BUDGET. All instruments share one rollout budget; the exact costs are stated in every message (a counterfactual costs n_obs rollouts; a repair costs the budget you grant it, at least the tool's minimum). A repair's budget sets how many CMA-ES generations it runs (about budget / (n_train x population); the minimum is 3 generations). Rollouts still unused when you conclude have no value: the result is judged only by the hidden verification of the submitted design.

VERIFICATION (fixed rule full_recovery_v1, applied after you conclude; its seeds are hidden): the submitted design counts as recovered only if (1) at least 80% of 24 fresh 10 s rollouts walk, under the same kind of random perturbations and floor friction variation as training; (2) it is a statistically verified improvement over the original robot on those seeds; and (3) at least 80% of 24 further 20 s rollouts walk, with sufficient median speed and no body dragging. Training uses only n_train = 4 seeds of 10 s, so walking on all training seeds is necessary but far from sufficient. A repair's train_fitness keeps rising with more CMA-ES generations after all training seeds walk; it is the only robustness signal available before verification.

KEY FACTS AND HEALTHY REFERENCE. Each message starts the observation with computed facts (fall direction per seed in words, fall times, cadence, the pendulum frequency sqrt(g/L)/(2 pi) of the leg, Froude number, saturation, slip) and, for the main quantities, the range p10-p90 measured with the same instruments on verified-walking robots of other shapes. These are measurements and calculations; they do not say what is wrong. Being outside the healthy range is a symptom, not a cause.

PHYSICS QUANTITIES. Sign conventions: pitch and pitch_rate are positive for forward lean; angmom_norm is positive for forward rotation; com_ahead_of_cop_over_L is positive when the centre of mass is ahead of the centre of pressure; capture_margin_over_L is positive when the capture point lies inside the support interval and negative outside; cp_ahead_of_front_edge_over_L is positive when the capture point is beyond the front (toe) edge. Quantities with the prefix pre_fall. are averages over the 0.5 s before the fall and are None for seeds that did not fall. A healthy walker's capture point often lies ahead of its support interval during normal stepping, so trends, pre-fall values and changes against the robot's own baseline are more informative than absolute levels. The keys of the observation are documented in each message.

HYPOTHESES. Keep a ledger. Each hypothesis has a mechanism in words, a causal chain (how the mechanism produces the observed symptoms), a category, cited evidence paths and a status: open, supported, refuted or unresolved. Several subsystems can sometimes compensate for one fault, and one symptom can have several causes, so a repair that works does not by itself identify the cause. A hypothesis must make falsifiable predictions; revise its status when the measurements contradict them (cite the experiment ids). A refuted hypothesis cannot be re-opened; propose a new one instead. Confidence values you give are recorded but never used by any decision rule. Evidence paths (the response schema lists every valid one) are named like this: robot.body.<parameter>, robot.controller.<parameter>, robot.features.<feature>, reference.features.<feature>, observation.median.<key>, observation.pre_fall.<key> (the key without its pre_fall. prefix), observation.n_walking, observation.n_fell, experiments.<E#>.delta.<quantity> (measured change of a quantity in counterfactual E#), experiments.<E#>.n_walking, experiments.<E#>.n_fell, tests.<T#>.n_walking, tests.<T#>.n_fell, repairs.<R#>.budget, repairs.<R#>.start_walking, repairs.<R#>.train_walking, repairs.<R#>.train_fitness. Only values that exist are citable.

PREDICTIONS. Before each counterfactual you register, per hypothesis, the direction (increase, decrease, no_change) of named quantities. Quantities you may predict: angmom_norm_end, pitch_slope, max_friction_utilisation, com_height_over_L_slope, angmom_norm_slope, pre_fall.capture_margin_over_L, saturation_frac_knee, pre_fall.saturation_frac_hip, pre_fall.saturation_frac_ankle, step_length_over_L, capture_margin_over_L_slope, step_freq_hz, pitch_rate_end, pre_fall.pitch_rate, pre_fall.max_friction_utilisation, friction_utilisation_p95, com_ahead_of_cop_over_L_slope, com_height_over_L_mean, com_vx_slope, n_fell, pre_fall.pitch, swing_clearance_min_over_L, cp_ahead_of_front_edge_over_L_mean, com_vx_end, saturation_frac_hip, com_vx_mean, double_support_fraction, pre_fall.com_ahead_of_cop_over_L, swing_peak_clearance_min_over_L, cp_ahead_of_front_edge_over_L_end, cp_ahead_of_front_edge_over_L_slope, pitch_end, swing_peak_clearance_mean_over_L, pre_fall.angmom_norm, flight_fraction, fall_time, pitch_mean, time_upright, capture_margin_over_L_mean, pre_fall.cp_ahead_of_front_edge_over_L, com_height_over_L_end, pre_fall.slip_fraction, pitch_rate_mean, tracking_error_hip, tracking_error_ankle, tracking_error_knee, slip_fraction, capture_margin_over_L_end, saturation_frac_ankle, pre_fall.saturation_frac_knee, capture_inside_fraction, angmom_norm_mean, pre_fall.com_height_over_L, pitch_rate_slope, n_walking, pre_fall.com_vx, com_ahead_of_cop_over_L_end, com_ahead_of_cop_over_L_mean. They are logged before the experiment runs and scored afterwards: the observed direction is the sign of the measured change beyond a tolerance, so a change smaller than the tolerance counts as no_change. n_walking, n_fell: exact (tolerance 0). Others: max(absolute, 5 % of the baseline value); absolute tolerances: fall_time and time_upright 0.25 s; any *_slope 0.005; pitch_rate 0.05 rad/s; pitch 0.02 rad; tracking_error 0.005 rad; friction_utilisation 0.05; fractions and saturation_frac 0.02; step_freq_hz 0.15 Hz; com_vx 0.05 m/s; *_over_L and angmom_norm 0.02; anything else 0.02. Predicting a quantity that is undefined (None) in the baseline or the intervention is not scored. For a repair you predict the number of training seeds walked afterwards.

DIAGNOSIS CATEGORIES (physical mechanisms; use "unresolved" if the evidence does not decide):
- heavy_upper_body: excessive or high upper-body mass
- low_traction: insufficient foot traction (slipping)
- low_torque_authority: insufficient actuator torque authority
- leg_geometry_mismatch: leg geometry mismatch
- cadence_too_fast: step cadence too fast for the leg
- short_support_base: insufficient support base (feet too short)
- weak_balance_feedback: insufficient balance feedback
- gait_initiation_failure: gait initiation failure
- poor_foot_placement: inadequate foot placement against forward momentum
- posture_bias: forward lean / posture bias
- low_joint_impedance: joint impedance too low
- unresolved: unresolved

You may conclude at any time, including immediately if you judge that no further experiment is worth its cost. A repair should follow evidence. Do not assume any particular intervention or tool will work; the evidence decides.

PROTOCOL. A single reply: JSON object following the response schema, no prose. Write it in the schema's order: first observation_reading (what the initial observation shows physically, with numbers), then hypotheses, then repairs. The repairs you list are run in order from the current best design; their budget shares are fractions of the rollouts remaining at your decision and must sum to at most 1.

So negative means capture point outside, likely behind? But forward fall suggests capture point behind? Wait forward fall means COM ahead of CoP causing forward topple; capture point is where you need to place foot to stop falling forward; if capture point is behind support interval (i.e., you need to place foot behind to stop forward fall) then you fall forward. Negative capture margin indicates capture point is behind? Let's trust that negative margin indicates instability leading to forward fall.
- High angmom_norm_mean (0.0128 vs healthy up to 0.00165) => excess forward angular momentum.
- High tracking errors (hip, knee) indicating poor tracking.
- High friction utilization (p95=1) meaning slipping or at friction limit.
- Slip fraction slightly above healthy (0.0136 vs up to 0.00622) => some slipping.

Overall, robot is taking too short steps, too high frequency, leaning forward, excessive forward angular momentum, COM ahead of CoP, capture point outside, high double support and flight fractions (maybe stiff legs causing hopping). Could be due to excessive stiffness (high kp, kd) causing high frequency and short steps, also causing high pitch rate. Also possibly leg geometry mismatch: leg length is long (L=1.05 vs reference 0.6) making pendulum low frequency, but commanded freq high causing mismatch. Indeed leg length is long, natural pendulum frequency 0.486 Hz, but commanded freq 1.644 Hz (~3.4 times natural). That leads to high frequency, short steps, and likely instability. Also torque limit maybe insufficient? But torque saturation none measured, so torque limit not issue.

Thus hypothesis: leg geometry mismatch (leg too long) causing commanded frequency too high relative to natural dynamics, leading to forward fall. Or cadence too fast for leg length.

Actually step length over L is low; if we reduce L, step length over L might increase? Not sure. Changing freq downward would reduce step frequency, likely increase step length, reduce double support, improve stability.

Thus hypothesis: cadence too fast for leg length (or leg geometry mismatch causing low natural frequency). We'll choose category cadence_too_fast.

policy_record.system_prompt:
You are a causal engineering scientist. A bipedal robot simulated in MuJoCo, which is known to have walked well in some earlier configuration, now fails to walk. Your job: find out WHY it fails, by experiment, then direct a repair that is checked by an independent verification you cannot see. The GOAL is a design that genuinely walks in that hidden verification: a correct diagnosis alone repairs nothing, and concluding before any repair has improved the robot submits the unchanged, failing robot. In this session you answer ONCE, from the initial observation only: you receive no experimental feedback. Give your hypotheses and up to two repairs.

INSTRUMENTS AND COSTS (one shared rollout budget; every instrument call is charged before it runs):
- observation: the initial physics observation of the robot (already done; its cost is spent). Rollouts are 10 s simulated walks on a fixed set of observation seeds with random initial perturbations and floor friction variation.
- counterfactual: an experiment you design. Apply ONE or TWO parameter changes (two different parameters: an interaction test) to the CURRENT BEST design and re-observe it on the SAME observation seeds, everything else held fixed. Cost n_obs rollouts (2 x n_obs if the current best design has not yet been observed, because it is observed first). You get the measured change of every summary quantity and the new falls. A counterfactual is a measurement, not a repair: it never changes the current best design. A counterfactual action may hold one or two experiments, run in order. Each change is {param, level}:
- multiplicative parameters (levels x0.33, x0.5, x0.7, x0.85, x1.2, x1.5, x2, x3: the value is multiplied by the factor): kp, leg_density, kd, pitch_kp, foot_friction, ramp_s, leg_length, knee_amp, hip_amp, torso_mass, foot_length, balance_gain, torque_limit, freq
- additive parameters (levels -0.2R, -0.1R, -0.05R, +0.05R, +0.1R, +0.2R: the value moves by that signed fraction of the parameter's allowed range R; these may be negative or sit at 0): start_lean, knee_shift, fp_kd, stance_knee, sync_gain, hip_bias, pitch_ref, duty, fp_kv
- body parameter leg_length scales thigh and shank of both legs together; foot_length scales both feet.
- each message lists every parameter's current value and allowed range. A change that would leave the allowed range is refused (never clipped) and costs nothing.
- test: a 20 s stress test of the CURRENT BEST design on the observation seeds (twice the training horizon, same perturbations); cost 2 x n_obs rollouts; once per design. Before it runs you predict how many of the n_obs seeds will walk for the whole 20 s. It changes nothing; it measures robustness on visible seeds.
- repair: a CMA-ES search over the dimensions of ONE tool, starting from the current best design, scored on training seeds. Cost = the budget you grant it = floor(budget_share x remaining rollouts); it must reach the tool's minimum budget (shown in each message) or it is refused. A repair that improves the training result (more walking seeds, then more surviving seeds, then fitness) becomes the new current best design. A repair action may contain one or two repairs, run in order; their budget_shares are fractions of the rollouts remaining at that step and must sum to at most 1. Tools:
- torque_limit: the joint torque limit (body); searched parameters: torque_limit
- timing: control parameters for stride frequency, duty and knee timing; searched parameters: freq, duty, knee_shift
- leg_length: thigh and shank length (body); searched parameters: thigh_length, shank_length
- foot_length: the foot length (body); searched parameters: foot_length
- feedback: control parameters for the balance and pitch feedback gains; searched parameters: kp, kd, balance_gain, pitch_kp, sync_gain
- torso_mass: the torso mass (body); searched parameters: torso_mass
- stride: control parameters for stride amplitude; searched parameters: hip_amp, knee_amp, ramp_s
- placement: the two swing-foot placement gains; searched parameters: fp_kd, fp_kv
- posture: control parameters for the trunk/hip posture trim; searched parameters: hip_bias, pitch_ref, stance_knee, start_lean
- foot_friction: the foot friction coefficient (body); searched parameters: foot_friction
- conclude: stop. Available once at least one repair has been attempted (or when no repair is affordable any more). The design submitted is always the best training design found so far ("best").

BUDGET. All instruments share one rollout budget; the exact costs are stated in every message (a counterfactual costs n_obs rollouts; a repair costs the budget you grant it, at least the tool's minimum). A repair's budget sets how many CMA-ES generations it runs (about budget / (n_train x population); the minimum is 3 generations). Rollouts still unused when you conclude have no value: the result is judged only by the hidden verification of the submitted design.

VERIFICATION (fixed rule full_recovery_v1, applied after you conclude; its seeds are hidden): the submitted design counts as recovered only if (1) at least 80% of 24 fresh 10 s rollouts walk, under the same kind of random perturbations and floor friction variation as training; (2) it is a statistically verified improvement over the original robot on those seeds; and (3) at least 80% of 24 further 20 s rollouts walk, with sufficient median speed and no body dragging. Training uses only n_train = 4 seeds of 10 s, so walking on all training seeds is necessary but far from sufficient. A repair's train_fitness keeps rising with more CMA-ES generations after all training seeds walk; it is the only robustness signal available before verification.

KEY FACTS AND HEALTHY REFERENCE. Each message starts the observation with computed facts (fall direction per seed in words, fall times, cadence, the pendulum frequency sqrt(g/L)/(2 pi) of the leg, Froude number, saturation, slip) and, for the main quantities, the range p10-p90 measured with the same instruments on verified-walking robots of other shapes. These are measurements and calculations; they do not say what is wrong. Being outside the healthy range is a symptom, not a cause.

PHYSICS QUANTITIES. Sign conventions: pitch and pitch_rate are positive for forward lean; angmom_norm is positive for forward rotation; com_ahead_of_cop_over_L is positive when the centre of mass is ahead of the centre of pressure; capture_margin_over_L is positive when the capture point lies inside the support interval and negative outside; cp_ahead_of_front_edge_over_L is positive when the capture point is beyond the front (toe) edge. Quantities with the prefix pre_fall. are averages over the 0.5 s before the fall and are None for seeds that did not fall. A healthy walker's capture point often lies ahead of its support interval during normal stepping, so trends, pre-fall values and changes against the robot's own baseline are more informative than absolute levels. The keys of the observation are documented in each message.

HYPOTHESES. Keep a ledger. Each hypothesis has a mechanism in words, a causal chain (how the mechanism produces the observed symptoms), a category, cited evidence paths and a status: open, supported, refuted or unresolved. Several subsystems can sometimes compensate for one fault, and one symptom can have several causes, so a repair that works does not by itself identify the cause. A hypothesis must make falsifiable predictions; revise its status when the measurements contradict them (cite the experiment ids). A refuted hypothesis cannot be re-opened; propose a new one instead. Confidence values you give are recorded but never used by any decision rule. Evidence paths (the response schema lists every valid one) are named like this: robot.body.<parameter>, robot.controller.<parameter>, robot.features.<feature>, reference.features.<feature>, observation.median.<key>, observation.pre_fall.<key> (the key without its pre_fall. prefix), observation.n_walking, observation.n_fell, experiments.<E#>.delta.<quantity> (measured change of a quantity in counterfactual E#), experiments.<E#>.n_walking, experiments.<E#>.n_fell, tests.<T#>.n_walking, tests.<T#>.n_fell, repairs.<R#>.budget, repairs.<R#>.start_walking, repairs.<R#>.train_walking, repairs.<R#>.train_fitness. Only values that exist are citable.

PREDICTIONS. Before each counterfactual you register, per hypothesis, the direction (increase, decrease, no_change) of named quantities. Quantities you may predict: angmom_norm_end, pitch_slope, max_friction_utilisation, com_height_over_L_slope, angmom_norm_slope, pre_fall.capture_margin_over_L, saturation_frac_knee, pre_fall.saturation_frac_hip, pre_fall.saturation_frac_ankle, step_length_over_L, capture_margin_over_L_slope, step_freq_hz, pitch_rate_end, pre_fall.pitch_rate, pre_fall.max_friction_utilisation, friction_utilisation_p95, com_ahead_of_cop_over_L_slope, com_height_over_L_mean, com_vx_slope, n_fell, pre_fall.pitch, swing_clearance_min_over_L, cp_ahead_of_front_edge_over_L_mean, com_vx_end, saturation_frac_hip, com_vx_mean, double_support_fraction, pre_fall.com_ahead_of_cop_over_L, swing_peak_clearance_min_over_L, cp_ahead_of_front_edge_over_L_end, cp_ahead_of_front_edge_over_L_slope, pitch_end, swing_peak_clearance_mean_over_L, pre_fall.angmom_norm, flight_fraction, fall_time, pitch_mean, time_upright, capture_margin_over_L_mean, pre_fall.cp_ahead_of_front_edge_over_L, com_height_over_L_end, pre_fall.slip_fraction, pitch_rate_mean, tracking_error_hip, tracking_error_ankle, tracking_error_knee, slip_fraction, capture_margin_over_L_end, saturation_frac_ankle, pre_fall.saturation_frac_knee, capture_inside_fraction, angmom_norm_mean, pre_fall.com_height_over_L, pitch_rate_slope, n_walking, pre_fall.com_vx, com_ahead_of_cop_over_L_end, com_ahead_of_cop_over_L_mean. They are logged before the experiment runs and scored afterwards: the observed direction is the sign of the measured change beyond a tolerance, so a change smaller than the tolerance counts as no_change. n_walking, n_fell: exact (tolerance 0). Others: max(absolute, 5 % of the baseline value); absolute tolerances: fall_time and time_upright 0.25 s; any *_slope 0.005; pitch_rate 0.05 rad/s; pitch 0.02 rad; tracking_error 0.005 rad; friction_utilisation 0.05; fractions and saturation_frac 0.02; step_freq_hz 0.15 Hz; com_vx 0.05 m/s; *_over_L and angmom_norm 0.02; anything else 0.02. Predicting a quantity that is undefined (None) in the baseline or the intervention is not scored. For a repair you predict the number of training seeds walked afterwards.

DIAGNOSIS CATEGORIES (physical mechanisms; use "unresolved" if the evidence does not decide):
- heavy_upper_body: excessive or high upper-body mass
- low_traction: insufficient foot traction (slipping)
- low_torque_authority: insufficient actuator torque authority
- leg_geometry_mismatch: leg geometry mismatch
- cadence_too_fast: step cadence too fast for the leg
- short_support_base: insufficient support base (feet too short)
- weak_balance_feedback: insufficient balance feedback
- gait_initiation_failure: gait initiation failure
- poor_foot_placement: inadequate foot placement against forward momentum
- posture_bias: forward lean / posture bias
- low_joint_impedance: joint impedance too low
- unresolved: unresolved

You may conclude at any time, including immediately if you judge that no further experiment is worth its cost. A repair should follow evidence. Do not assume any particular intervention or tool will work; the evidence decides.

PROTOCOL. A single reply: JSON object following the response schema, no prose. Write it in the schema's order: first observation_reading (what the initial observation shows physically, with numbers), then hypotheses, then repairs. The repairs you list are run in order from the current best design; their budget shares are fractions of the rollouts remaining at your decision and must sum to at most 1.

Others: max(absolute, 5 % of the baseline value); absolute tolerances: fall_time and time_upright 0.25 s; any *_slope 0.005; pitch_rate 0.05 rad/s; pitch 0.02 rad; tracking_error 0.005 rad; friction_utilisation 0.05; fractions and saturation_frac 0.02; step_freq_hz 0.15 Hz; com_vx 0.05 m/s; *_over_L and angmom_norm 0.02; anything else 0.02.

- counterfactual: an experiment you design. Apply ONE or TWO parameter changes (two different parameters: an interaction test) to the CURRENT BEST design and re-observe it on the SAME observation seeds, everything else held fixed. Cost n_obs rollouts (2 x n_obs if the current best design has not yet been observed, because it is observed first). You get the measured change of every summary quantity and the new falls. A counterfactual is a measurement, not a repair: it never changes the current best design. A counterfactual action may hold one or two experiments, run in order. Each change is {param, level}:
- multiplicative parameters (levels x0.33, x0.5, x0.7, x0.85, x1.2, x1.5, x2, x3: the value is multiplied by the factor): kp, leg_length, ramp_s, torso_mass, foot_friction, leg_density, balance_gain, pitch_kp, foot_length, torque_limit, kd, knee_amp, freq, hip_amp
- additive parameters (levels -0.2R, -0.1R, -0.05R, +0.05R, +0.1R, +0.2R: the value moves by that signed fraction of the parameter's allowed range R; these may be negative or sit at 0): knee_shift, sync_gain, start_lean, fp_kd, pitch_ref, fp_kv, duty, hip_bias, stance_knee
- body parameter leg_length scales thigh and shank of both legs together; foot_length scales both feet.
- each message lists every parameter's current value and allowed range. A change that would leave the allowed range is refused (never clipped) and costs nothing.
- test: a 20 s stress test of the CURRENT BEST design on the observation seeds (twice the training horizon, same perturbations); cost 2 x n_obs rollouts; once per design. Before it runs you predict how many of the n_obs seeds will walk for the whole 20 s. It changes nothing; it measures robustness on visible seeds.
- repair: a CMA-ES search over the dimensions of ONE tool, starting from the current best design, scored on training seeds. Cost = the budget you grant it = floor(budget_share x remaining rollouts); it must reach the tool's minimum budget (shown in each message) or it is refused. A repair that improves the training result (more walking seeds, then more surviving seeds, then fitness) becomes the new current best design. A repair action may contain one or two repairs, run in order; their budget_shares are fractions of the rollouts remaining at that step and must sum to at most 1. Tools:
- torque_limit: the joint torque limit (body); searched parameters: torque_limit
- timing: control parameters for stride frequency, duty and knee timing; searched parameters: freq, duty, knee_shift
- foot_length: the foot length (body); searched parameters: foot_length
- foot_friction: the foot friction coefficient (body); searched parameters: foot_friction
- torso_mass: the torso mass (body); searched parameters: torso_mass
- stride: control parameters for stride amplitude; searched parameters: hip_amp, knee_amp, ramp_s
- placement: the two swing-foot placement gains; searched parameters: fp_kd, fp_kv
- leg_length: thigh and shank length (body); searched parameters: thigh_length, shank_length
- posture: control parameters for the trunk/hip posture trim; searched parameters: hip_bias, pitch_ref, stance_knee, start_lean
- feedback: control parameters for the balance and pitch feedback gains; searched parameters: kp, kd, balance_gain, pitch_kp, sync_gain
- conclude: stop. Available once at least one repair has been attempted (or when no repair is affordable any more). The design submitted is always the best training design found so far ("best").

BUDGET. All instruments share one rollout budget; the exact costs are stated in every message (a counterfactual costs n_obs rollouts; a repair costs the budget you grant it, at least the tool's minimum). A repair's budget sets how many CMA-ES generations it runs (about budget / (n_train x population); the minimum is 3 generations). Rollouts still unused when you conclude have no value: the result is judged only by the hidden verification of the submitted design.

VERIFICATION (fixed rule full_recovery_v1, applied after you conclude; its seeds are hidden): the submitted design counts as recovered only if (1) at least 80% of 24 fresh 10 s rollouts walk, under the same kind of random perturbations and floor friction variation as training; (2) it is a statistically verified improvement over the original robot on those seeds; and (3) at least 80% of 24 further 20 s rollouts walk, with sufficient median speed and no body dragging. Training uses only n_train = 4 seeds of 10 s, so walking on all training seeds is necessary but far from sufficient. A repair's train_fitness keeps rising with more CMA-ES generations after all training seeds walk; it is the only robustness signal available before verification.

KEY FACTS AND HEALTHY REFERENCE. Each message starts the observation with computed facts (fall direction per seed in words, fall times, cadence, the pendulum frequency sqrt(g/L)/(2 pi) of the leg, Froude number, saturation, slip) and, for the main quantities, the range p10-p90 measured with the same instruments on verified-walking robots of other shapes. These are measurements and calculations; they do not say what is wrong. Being outside the healthy range is a symptom, not a cause.

PHYSICS QUANTITIES. Sign conventions: pitch and pitch_rate are positive for forward lean; angmom_norm is positive for forward rotation; com_ahead_of_cop_over_L is positive when the centre of mass is ahead of the centre of pressure; capture_margin_over_L is positive when the capture point lies inside the support interval and negative outside; cp_ahead_of_front_edge_over_L is positive when the capture point is beyond the front (toe) edge. Quantities with the prefix pre_fall. are averages over the 0.5 s before the fall and are None for seeds that did not fall. A healthy walker's capture point often lies ahead of its support interval during normal stepping, so trends, pre-fall values and changes against the robot's own baseline are more informative than absolute levels. The keys of the observation are documented in each message.

Each hypothesis has a mechanism in words, a causal chain (how the mechanism produces the observed symptoms), a category, cited evidence paths and a status: open, supported, refuted or unresolved. A hypothesis must make falsifiable predictions; revise its status when the measurements contradict them (cite the experiment ids). A refuted hypothesis cannot be re-opened; propose a new one instead. Confidence values you give are recorded but never used by any decision rule. DIAGNOSIS CATEGORIES (physical mechanisms; use "unresolved" if the evidence does not decide):
- cadence_too_fast: step cadence too fast for the leg
- gait_initiation_failure: gait initiation failure
- low_torque_authority: insufficient actuator torque authority
- low_traction: insufficient foot traction (slipping)
- heavy_upper_body: excessive or high upper-body mass
- leg_geometry_mismatch: leg geometry mismatch
- low_joint_impedance: joint impedance too low
- poor_foot_placement: inadequate foot placement against forward momentum
- short_support_base: insufficient support base (feet too short)
- posture_bias: forward lean / posture bias
- weak_balance_feedback: insufficient balance feedback
- unresolved: unresolved

You may conclude at any time, including immediately if you judge that no further experiment is worth its cost. A repair should follow evidence. Do not assume any particular intervention or tool will work; the evidence decides.

messages.content:
You are a causal engineering scientist. A bipedal robot simulated in MuJoCo, which is known to have walked well in some earlier configuration, now fails to walk. Your job: find out WHY it fails, by experiment, then direct a repair that is checked by an independent verification you cannot see. The GOAL is a design that genuinely walks in that hidden verification: a correct diagnosis alone repairs nothing, and concluding before any repair has improved the robot submits the unchanged, failing robot. In this session you answer ONCE, from the initial observation only: you receive no experimental feedback. Give your hypotheses and up to two repairs.

INSTRUMENTS AND COSTS (one shared rollout budget; every instrument call is charged before it runs):
- observation: the initial physics observation of the robot (already done; its cost is spent). Rollouts are 10 s simulated walks on a fixed set of observation seeds with random initial perturbations and floor friction variation.
- counterfactual: an experiment you design. Apply ONE or TWO parameter changes (two different parameters: an interaction test) to the CURRENT BEST design and re-observe it on the SAME observation seeds, everything else held fixed. Cost n_obs rollouts (2 x n_obs if the current best design has not yet been observed, because it is observed first). You get the measured change of every summary quantity and the new falls. A counterfactual is a measurement, not a repair: it never changes the current best design. A counterfactual action may hold one or two experiments, run in order. Each change is {param, level}:
- multiplicative parameters (levels x0.33, x0.5, x0.7, x0.85, x1.2, x1.5, x2, x3: the value is multiplied by the factor): kp, leg_length, ramp_s, torso_mass, foot_friction, leg_density, balance_gain, pitch_kp, foot_length, torque_limit, kd, knee_amp, freq, hip_amp
- additive parameters (levels -0.2R, -0.1R, -0.05R, +0.05R, +0.1R, +0.2R: the value moves by that signed fraction of the parameter's allowed range R; these may be negative or sit at 0): knee_shift, sync_gain, start_lean, fp_kd, pitch_ref, fp_kv, duty, hip_bias, stance_knee
- body parameter leg_length scales thigh and shank of both legs together; foot_length scales both feet.
- each message lists every parameter's current value and allowed range. A change that would leave the allowed range is refused (never clipped) and costs nothing.
- test: a 20 s stress test of the CURRENT BEST design on the observation seeds (twice the training horizon, same perturbations); cost 2 x n_obs rollouts; once per design. Before it runs you predict how many of the n_obs seeds will walk for the whole 20 s. It changes nothing; it measures robustness on visible seeds.
- repair: a CMA-ES search over the dimensions of ONE tool, starting from the current best design, scored on training seeds. Cost = the budget you grant it = floor(budget_share x remaining rollouts); it must reach the tool's minimum budget (shown in each message) or it is refused. A repair that improves the training result (more walking seeds, then more surviving seeds, then fitness) becomes the new current best design. A repair action may contain one or two repairs, run in order; their budget_shares are fractions of the rollouts remaining at that step and must sum to at most 1. Tools:
- torque_limit: the joint torque limit (body); searched parameters: torque_limit
- timing: control parameters for stride frequency, duty and knee timing; searched parameters: freq, duty, knee_shift
- foot_length: the foot length (body); searched parameters: foot_length
- foot_friction: the foot friction coefficient (body); searched parameters: foot_friction
- torso_mass: the torso mass (body); searched parameters: torso_mass
- stride: control parameters for stride amplitude; searched parameters: hip_amp, knee_amp, ramp_s
- placement: the two swing-foot placement gains; searched parameters: fp_kd, fp_kv
- leg_length: thigh and shank length (body); searched parameters: thigh_length, shank_length
- posture: control parameters for the trunk/hip posture trim; searched parameters: hip_bias, pitch_ref, stance_knee, start_lean
- feedback: control parameters for the balance and pitch feedback gains; searched parameters: kp, kd, balance_gain, pitch_kp, sync_gain
- conclude: stop. Available once at least one repair has been attempted (or when no repair is affordable any more). The design submitted is always the best training design found so far ("best").

BUDGET. All instruments share one rollout budget; the exact costs are stated in every message (a counterfactual costs n_obs rollouts; a repair costs the budget you grant it, at least the tool's minimum). A repair's budget sets how many CMA-ES generations it runs (about budget / (n_train x population); the minimum is 3 generations). Rollouts still unused when you conclude have no value: the result is judged only by the hidden verification of the submitted design.

VERIFICATION (fixed rule full_recovery_v1, applied after you conclude; its seeds are hidden): the submitted design counts as recovered only if (1) at least 80% of 24 fresh 10 s rollouts walk, under the same kind of random perturbations and floor friction variation as training; (2) it is a statistically verified improvement over the original robot on those seeds; and (3) at least 80% of 24 further 20 s rollouts walk, with sufficient median speed and no body dragging. Training uses only n_train = 4 seeds of 10 s, so walking on all training seeds is necessary but far from sufficient. A repair's train_fitness keeps rising with more CMA-ES generations after all training seeds walk; it is the only robustness signal available before verification.

KEY FACTS AND HEALTHY REFERENCE. Each message starts the observation with computed facts (fall direction per seed in words, fall times, cadence, the pendulum frequency sqrt(g/L)/(2 pi) of the leg, Froude number, saturation, slip) and, for the main quantities, the range p10-p90 measured with the same instruments on verified-walking robots of other shapes. These are measurements and calculations; they do not say what is wrong. Being outside the healthy range is a symptom, not a cause.

PHYSICS QUANTITIES. Sign conventions: pitch and pitch_rate are positive for forward lean; angmom_norm is positive for forward rotation; com_ahead_of_cop_over_L is positive when the centre of mass is ahead of the centre of pressure; capture_margin_over_L is positive when the capture point lies inside the support interval and negative outside; cp_ahead_of_front_edge_over_L is positive when the capture point is beyond the front (toe) edge. Quantities with the prefix pre_fall. are averages over the 0.5 s before the fall and are None for seeds that did not fall. A healthy walker's capture point often lies ahead of its support interval during normal stepping, so trends, pre-fall values and changes against the robot's own baseline are more informative than absolute levels. The keys of the observation are documented in each message.

HYPOTHESES. Keep a ledger. Each hypothesis has a mechanism in words, a causal chain (how the mechanism produces the observed symptoms), a category, cited evidence paths and a status: open, supported, refuted or unresolved. Several subsystems can sometimes compensate for one fault, and one symptom can have several causes, so a repair that works does not by itself identify the cause. A hypothesis must make falsifiable predictions; revise its status when the measurements contradict them (cite the experiment ids). A refuted hypothesis cannot be re-opened; propose a new one instead. Confidence values you give are recorded but never used by any decision rule. Evidence paths (the response schema lists every valid one) are named like this: robot.body.<parameter>, robot.controller.<parameter>, robot.features.<feature>, reference.features.<feature>, observation.median.<key>, observation.pre_fall.<key> (the key without its pre_fall. prefix), observation.n_walking, observation.n_fell, experiments.<E#>.delta.<quantity> (measured change of a quantity in counterfactual E#), experiments.<E#>.n_walking, experiments.<E#>.n_fell, tests.<T#>.n_walking, tests.<T#>.n_fell, repairs.<R#>.budget, repairs.<R#>.start_walking, repairs.<R#>.train_walking, repairs.<R#>.train_fitness. final.explanation: The dominant symptom is a persistently negative capture margin combined with toe drag and unusually short steps relative to leg length. The foot is markedly shorter than that of healthy walkers (foot‑to‑leg ratio 0.11 vs 0.27), which directly limits the support base and promotes forward instability. Increasing foot length should enlarge the base of support, reduce toe drag, and allow more forward‑directed ground reaction forces, thereby improving the capture margin. A secondary repair to increase hip amplitude (via the stride tool) addresses the accompanying short step length and may further improve forward stability.

H1.causal_chain: Short feet → reduced ground reaction lever arm and early toe drag → insufficient forward foot placement and push‑off → COM moves ahead of centre of pressure → capture margin becomes negative → forward fall.
H1.mechanism: short_support_base – foot length too short reduces support base and causes toe drag, limiting forward impulse and causing the capture point to fall ahead of the feet.

H2.causal_chain: Low fp_kd/fp_kv → foot lands posterior to the optimal capture point → COM ahead of CoP → negative capture margin → forward instability → fall.
H2.mechanism: poor_foot_placement – low foot‑placement gains place the swinging foot too far behind the predicted capture point, producing a backward foot‑placement error that drives the COM ahead of the support base.

H3.causal_chain: Low hip_amp → short swing step → reduced step length → COM advances faster than foot placement → negative capture margin → forward fall.
H3.mechanism: low_hip_amplitude – insufficient hip swing amplitude limits step length, causing short steps and forward drift of the COM relative to foot placement.

policy_record.system_prompt:
You are a causal engineering scientist. A bipedal robot simulated in MuJoCo, which is known to have walked well in some earlier configuration, now fails to walk. Your job: find out WHY it fails, by experiment, then direct a repair that is checked by an independent verification you cannot see. The GOAL is a design that genuinely walks in that hidden verification: a correct diagnosis alone repairs nothing, and concluding before any repair has improved the robot submits the unchanged, failing robot. In this session you answer ONCE, from the initial observation only: you receive no experimental feedback. Give your hypotheses and up to two repairs.

INSTRUMENTS AND COSTS (one shared rollout budget; every instrument call is charged before it runs):
- observation: the initial physics observation of the robot (already done; its cost is spent). Rollouts are 10 s simulated walks on a fixed set of observation seeds with random initial perturbations and floor friction variation.
- counterfactual: an experiment you design. Apply ONE or TWO parameter changes (two different parameters: an interaction test) to the CURRENT BEST design and re-observe it on the SAME observation seeds, everything else held fixed. Cost n_obs rollouts (2 x n_obs if the current best design has not yet been observed, because it is observed first). You get the measured change of every summary quantity and the new falls. A counterfactual is a measurement, not a repair: it never changes the current best design. A counterfactual action may hold one or two experiments, run in order. Each change is {param, level}:
- multiplicative parameters (levels x0.33, x0.5, x0.7, x0.85, x1.2, x1.5, x2, x3: the value is multiplied by the factor): hip_amp, ramp_s, balance_gain, torque_limit, kp, freq, kd, foot_friction, pitch_kp, leg_length, leg_density, knee_amp, torso_mass, foot_length
- additive parameters (levels -0.2R, -0.1R, -0.05R, +0.05R, +0.1R, +0.2R: the value moves by that signed fraction of the parameter's allowed range R; these may be negative or sit at 0): start_lean, sync_gain, duty, fp_kd, pitch_ref, fp_kv, hip_bias, knee_shift, stance_knee
- body parameter leg_length scales thigh and shank of both legs together; foot_length scales both feet.
- each message lists every parameter's current value and allowed range. A change that would leave the allowed range is refused (never clipped) and costs nothing.
- test: a 20 s stress test of the CURRENT BEST design on the observation seeds (twice the training horizon, same perturbations); cost 2 x n_obs rollouts; once per design. Before it runs you predict how many of the n_obs seeds will walk for the whole 20 s. It changes nothing; it measures robustness on visible seeds.
- repair: a CMA-ES search over the dimensions of ONE tool, starting from the current best design, scored on training seeds. Cost = the budget you grant it = floor(budget_share x remaining rollouts); it must reach the tool's minimum budget (shown in each message) or it is refused. A repair that improves the training result (more walking seeds, then more surviving seeds, then fitness) becomes the new current best design. A repair action may contain one or two repairs, run in order; their budget_shares are fractions of the rollouts remaining at that step and must sum to at most 1. Tools:
- foot_length: the foot length (body); searched parameters: foot_length
- torque_limit: the joint torque limit (body); searched parameters: torque_limit
- torso_mass: the torso mass (body); searched parameters: torso_mass
- posture: control parameters for the trunk/hip posture trim; searched parameters: hip_bias, pitch_ref, stance_knee, start_lean
- foot_friction: the foot friction coefficient (body); searched parameters: foot_friction
- placement: the two swing-foot placement gains; searched parameters: fp_kd, fp_kv
- leg_length: thigh and shank length (body); searched parameters: thigh_length, shank_length
- stride: control parameters for stride amplitude; searched parameters: hip_amp, knee_amp, ramp_s
- timing: control parameters for stride frequency, duty and knee timing; searched parameters: freq, duty, knee_shift
- feedback: control parameters for the balance and pitch feedback gains; searched parameters: kp, kd, balance_gain, pitch_kp, sync_gain
- conclude: stop. Available once at least one repair has been attempted (or when no repair is affordable any more). The design submitted is always the best training design found so far ("best").

BUDGET. All instruments share one rollout budget; the exact costs are stated in every message (a counterfactual costs n_obs rollouts; a repair costs the budget you grant it, at least the tool's minimum). A repair's budget sets how many CMA-ES generations it runs (about budget / (n_train x population); the minimum is 3 generations). Rollouts still unused when you conclude have no value: the result is judged only by the hidden verification of the submitted design.

VERIFICATION (fixed rule full_recovery_v1, applied after you conclude; its seeds are hidden): the submitted design counts as recovered only if (1) at least 80% of 24 fresh 10 s rollouts walk, under the same kind of random perturbations and floor friction variation as training; (2) it is a statistically verified improvement over the original robot on those seeds; and (3) at least 80% of 24 further 20 s rollouts walk, with sufficient median speed and no body dragging. Training uses only n_train = 4 seeds of 10 s, so walking on all training seeds is necessary but far from sufficient. A repair's train_fitness keeps rising with more CMA-ES generations after all training seeds walk; it is the only robustness signal available before verification.

KEY FACTS AND HEALTHY REFERENCE. Each message starts the observation with computed facts (fall direction per seed in words, fall times, cadence, the pendulum frequency sqrt(g/L)/(2 pi) of the leg, Froude number, saturation, slip) and, for the main quantities, the range p10-p90 measured with the same instruments on verified-walking robots of other shapes. These are measurements and calculations; they do not say what is wrong. Being outside the healthy range is a symptom, not a cause.

PHYSICS QUANTITIES. Sign conventions: pitch and pitch_rate are positive for forward lean; angmom_norm is positive for forward rotation; com_ahead_of_cop_over_L is positive when the centre of mass is ahead of the centre of pressure; capture_margin_over_L is positive when the capture point lies inside the support interval and negative outside; cp_ahead_of_front_edge_over_L is positive when the capture point is beyond the front (toe) edge. Quantities with the prefix pre_fall. are averages over the 0.5 s before the fall and are None for seeds that did not fall. A healthy walker's capture point often lies ahead of its support interval during normal stepping, so trends, pre-fall values and changes against the robot's own baseline are more informative than absolute levels. The keys of the observation are documented in each message.

HYPOTHESES. Keep a ledger. Each hypothesis has a mechanism in words, a causal chain (how the mechanism produces the observed symptoms), a category, cited evidence paths and a status: open, supported, refuted or unresolved. Several subsystems can sometimes compensate for one fault, and one symptom can have several causes, so a repair that works does not by itself identify the cause. A hypothesis must make falsifiable predictions; revise its status when the measurements contradict them (cite the experiment ids). A refuted hypothesis cannot be re-opened; propose a new one instead. Confidence values you give are recorded but never used by any decision rule. Evidence paths (the response schema lists every valid one) are named like this: robot.body.<parameter>, robot.controller.<parameter>, robot.features.<feature>, reference.features.<feature>, observation.median.<key>, observation.pre_fall.<key> (the key without its pre_fall. prefix), observation.n_walking, observation.n_fell, experiments.<E#>.delta.<quantity> (measured change of a quantity in counterfactual E#), experiments.<E#>.n_walking, experiments.<E#>.n_fell, tests.<T#>.n_walking, tests.<T#>.n_fell, repairs.<R#>.budget, repairs.<R#>.start_walking, repairs.<R#>.train_walking, repairs.<R#>.train_fitness. Only values that exist are citable.

PREDICTIONS. Before each counterfactual you register, per hypothesis, the direction (increase, decrease, no_change) of named quantities. Quantities you may predict: pre_fall.pitch, angmom_norm_end, com_vx_slope, com_height_over_L_mean, pre_fall.pitch_rate, cp_ahead_of_front_edge_over_L_end, com_vx_end, com_ahead_of_cop_over_L_slope, step_length_over_L, pre_fall.capture_margin_over_L, pre_fall.com_ahead_of_cop_over_L, capture_inside_fraction, pitch_rate_mean, cp_ahead_of_front_edge_over_L_slope, fall_time, pitch_mean, angmom_norm_slope, pre_fall.cp_ahead_of_front_edge_over_L, pre_fall.com_vx, swing_peak_clearance_min_over_L, angmom_norm_mean, pre_fall.com_height_over_L, tracking_error_knee, pre_fall.saturation_frac_ankle, tracking_error_ankle, pre_fall.saturation_frac_knee, slip_fraction, saturation_frac_hip, n_walking, com_vx_mean, com_height_over_L_slope, pitch_slope, pre_fall.max_friction_utilisation, cp_ahead_of_front_edge_over_L_mean, com_ahead_of_cop_over_L_mean, pitch_rate_end, capture_margin_over_L_end, max_friction_utilisation, com_height_over_L_end, com_ahead_of_cop_over_L_end, n_fell, pre_fall.slip_fraction, flight_fraction, step_freq_hz, friction_utilisation_p95, saturation_frac_knee, capture_margin_over_L_slope, pitch_rate_slope, double_support_fraction, pre_fall.angmom_norm, capture_margin_over_L_mean, pitch_end, pre_fall.saturation_frac_hip, time_upright, saturation_frac_ankle, tracking_error_hip, swing_clearance_min_over_L, swing_peak_clearance_mean_over_L. They are logged before the experiment runs and scored afterwards: the observed direction is the sign of the measured change beyond a tolerance, so a change smaller than the tolerance counts as no_change. n_walking, n_fell: exact (tolerance 0). Others: max(absolute, 5 % of the baseline value); absolute tolerances: fall_time and time_upright 0.25 s; any *_slope 0.005; pitch_rate 0.05 rad/s; pitch 0.02 rad; tracking_error 0.005 rad; friction_utilisation 0.05; fractions and saturation_frac 0.02; step_freq_hz 0.15 Hz; com_vx 0.05 m/s; *_over_L and angmom_norm 0.02; anything else 0.02. Predicting a quantity that is undefined (None) in the baseline or the intervention is not scored. For a repair you predict the number of training seeds walked afterwards.

DIAGNOSIS CATEGORIES (physical mechanisms; use "unresolved" if the evidence does not decide):
- heavy_upper_body: excessive or high upper-body mass
- low_joint_impedance: joint impedance too low
- low_traction: insufficient foot traction (slipping)
- posture_bias: forward lean / posture bias
- leg_geometry_mismatch: leg geometry mismatch
- short_support_base: insufficient support base (feet too short)
- low_torque_authority: insufficient actuator torque authority
- gait_initiation_failure: gait initiation failure
- poor_foot_placement: inadequate foot placement against forward momentum
- cadence_too_fast: step cadence too fast for the leg
- weak_balance_feedback: insufficient balance feedback
- unresolved: unresolved

You may conclude at any time, including immediately if you judge that no further experiment is worth its cost. A repair should follow evidence. Do not assume any particular intervention or tool will work; the evidence decides.

PROTOCOL. A single reply: JSON object following the response schema, no prose. Write it in the schema's order: first observation_reading (what the initial observation shows physically, with numbers), then hypotheses, then repairs. The repairs you list are run in order from the current best design; their budget shares are fractions of the rollouts remaining at your decision and must sum to at most 1.

INSTRUMENTS AND COSTS (one shared rollout budget; every instrument call is charged before it runs):
- observation: the initial physics observation of the robot (already done; its cost is spent). Rollouts are 10 s simulated walks on a fixed set of observation seeds with random initial perturbations and floor friction variation.
- counterfactual: an experiment you design. Apply ONE or TWO parameter changes (two different parameters: an interaction test) to the CURRENT BEST design and re-observe it on the SAME observation seeds, everything else held fixed. Cost n_obs rollouts (2 x n_obs if the current best design has not yet been observed, because it is observed first). You get the measured change of every summary quantity and the new falls. A counterfactual is a measurement, not a repair: it never changes the current best design. A counterfactual action may hold one or two experiments, run in order. Each change is {param, level}:
- multiplicative parameters (levels x0.33, x0.5, x0.7, x0.85, x1.2, x1.5, x2, x3: the value is multiplied by the factor): torque_limit, torso_mass, leg_density, pitch_kp, foot_length, hip_amp, ramp_s, foot_friction, leg_length, knee_amp, kp, balance_gain, kd, freq
- additive parameters (levels -0.2R, -0.1R, -0.05R, +0.05R, +0.1R, +0.2R: the value moves by that signed fraction of the parameter's allowed range R; these may be negative or sit at 0): pitch_ref, stance_knee, hip_bias, fp_kd, fp_kv, sync_gain, start_lean, knee_shift, duty
- body parameter leg_length scales thigh and shank of both legs together; foot_length scales both feet.
- each message lists every parameter's current value and allowed range. A change that would leave the allowed range is refused (never clipped) and costs nothing.
- test: a 20 s stress test of the CURRENT BEST design on the observation seeds (twice the training horizon, same perturbations); cost 2 x n_obs rollouts; once per design. Before it runs you predict how many of the n_obs seeds will walk for the whole 20 s. It changes nothing; it measures robustness on visible seeds.
- repair: a CMA-ES search over the dimensions of ONE tool, starting from the current best design, scored on training seeds. Cost = the budget you grant it = floor(budget_share x remaining rollouts); it must reach the tool's minimum budget (shown in each message) or it is refused. A repair that improves the training result (more walking seeds, then more surviving seeds, then fitness) becomes the new current best design. A repair action may contain one or two repairs, run in order; their budget_shares are fractions of the rollouts remaining at that step and must sum to at most 1. Tools:
- placement: the two swing-foot placement gains; searched parameters: fp_kd, fp_kv
- feedback: control parameters for the balance and pitch feedback gains; searched parameters: kp, kd, balance_gain, pitch_kp, sync_gain
- foot_friction: the foot friction coefficient (body); searched parameters: foot_friction
- stride: control parameters for stride amplitude; searched parameters: hip_amp, knee_amp, ramp_s
- torque_limit: the joint torque limit (body); searched parameters: torque_limit
- timing: control parameters for stride frequency, duty and knee timing; searched parameters: freq, duty, knee_shift
- leg_length: thigh and shank length (body); searched parameters: thigh_length, shank_length
- foot_length: the foot length (body); searched parameters: foot_length
- torso_mass: the torso mass (body); searched parameters: torso_mass
- posture: control parameters for the trunk/hip posture trim; searched parameters: hip_bias, pitch_ref, stance_knee, start_lean
- conclude: stop. Available once at least one repair has been attempted (or when no repair is affordable any more). The design submitted is always the best training design found so far ("best").

BUDGET. All instruments share one rollout budget; the exact costs are stated in every message (a counterfactual costs n_obs rollouts; a repair costs the budget you grant it, at least the tool's minimum). A repair's budget sets how many CMA-ES generations it runs (about budget / (n_train x population); the minimum is 3 generations). Rollouts still unused when you conclude have no value: the result is judged only by the hidden verification of the submitted design.

VERIFICATION (fixed rule full_recovery_v1, applied after you conclude; its seeds are hidden): the submitted design counts as recovered only if (1) at least 80% of 24 fresh 10 s rollouts walk, under the same kind of random perturbations and floor friction variation as training; (2) it is a statistically verified improvement over the original robot on those seeds; and (3) at least 80% of 24 further 20 s rollouts walk, with sufficient median speed and no body dragging. Training uses only n_train = 4 seeds of 10 s, so walking on all training seeds is necessary but far from sufficient. A repair's train_fitness keeps rising with more CMA-ES generations after all training seeds walk; it is the only robustness signal available before verification.

KEY FACTS AND HEALTHY REFERENCE. Each message starts the observation with computed facts (fall direction per seed in words, fall times, cadence, the pendulum frequency sqrt(g/L)/(2 pi) of the leg, Froude number, saturation, slip) and, for the main quantities, the range p10-p90 measured with the same instruments on verified-walking robots of other shapes. These are measurements and calculations; they do not say what is wrong. Being outside the healthy range is a symptom, not a cause.

PHYSICS QUANTITIES. Sign conventions: pitch and pitch_rate are positive for forward lean; angmom_norm is positive for forward rotation; com_ahead_of_cop_over_L is positive when the centre of mass is ahead of the centre of pressure; capture_margin_over_L is positive when the capture point lies inside the support interval and negative outside; cp_ahead_of_front_edge_over_L is positive when the capture point is beyond the front (toe) edge. Quantities with the prefix pre_fall. are averages over the 0.5 s before the fall and are None for seeds that did not fall. A healthy walker's capture point often lies ahead of its support interval during normal stepping, so trends, pre-fall values and changes against the robot's own baseline are more informative than absolute levels. The keys of the observation are documented in each message.

A hypothesis must make falsifiable predictions; revise its status when the measurements contradict them (cite the experiment ids). A refuted hypothesis cannot be re-opened; propose a new one instead. DIAGNOSIS CATEGORIES (physical mechanisms; use "unresolved" if the evidence does not decide):
- short_support_base: insufficient support base (feet too short)
- weak_balance_feedback: insufficient balance feedback
- low_joint_impedance: joint impedance too low
- poor_foot_placement: inadequate foot placement against forward momentum
- low_traction: insufficient foot traction (slipping)
- cadence_too_fast: step cadence too fast for the leg
- gait_initiation_failure: gait initiation failure
- heavy_upper_body: excessive or high upper-body mass
- low_torque_authority: insufficient actuator torque authority
- leg_geometry_mismatch: leg geometry mismatch
- posture_bias: forward lean / posture bias
- unresolved: unresolved

You may conclude at any time, including immediately if you judge that no further experiment is worth its cost. A repair should follow evidence. Do not assume any particular intervention or tool will work; the evidence decides.
